simple.meaning: תֻּמִּים (Tummîym) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “perfections , i.e. (techn.) one of the epithets of the objects in the high-priest's breastplate as an emblem of complete Truth.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Exodus, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Ezra, Nehemiah, beginning at Exodus 28:30. Its contexts include priesthood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תֻּמִּים (H8550).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: תֻּמִּים (Tummîym) / H8550 is traced through Exodus 28:30, Leviticus 8:8, Deuteronomy 33:8, Ezra 2:63 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: perfections , i.e. (techn.) one of the epithets of the objects in the high-priest's breastplate as an emblem of complete Truth

firstOccurrence.englishText: You shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be on Aaron’s heart, when he goes in before Yahweh. Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel on his heart before Yahweh continually.

timeline.evidenceText: You shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be on Aaron’s heart, when he goes in before Yahweh. Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel on his heart before Yahweh continually.
He placed the breastplate on him. He put the Urim and Thummim in the breastplate.
The governor told them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to serve with Urim and with Thummim.
The governor told that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stood up to minister with Urim and Thummim.
